trickyParts: Two branches open at once each restated graph_edges from 0142's arms. Timestamps sort main's 20261101144855 after this branch's 20261101143211, so main's view silently replaced the ask arms and no conflict marker said so. The fix is a third migration stating the view once from both arm lists; renaming this branch's migrations was rejected (it defeats timestamped versions and churns every citation) and editing main's applied migration is unsafe for any database that ran it.
A text merge of refs/ask_blocks.go kept both call shapes of blockPairs, which does not compile. A merge resolution is not proven by its conflict markers being gone: the build is the check.

The block[] refusal has no reachable HTTP surface on a stock build, because no shipped block type declares a block[] attribute (packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:1679, and GET /api/v1/schema/blocks lists none). Driving the three write paths needed a server built with the Go tests' schema through one untracked file, since deleted. Without such a schema the standing guard is the twin corpora alone.
deviations: The architect's acceptance line for T7 said 400 INVALID_MARKDOWN on all three write paths. That holds for an upload alone. An edit op answers 400 INVALID_OP on the op's field, by docs/edits.go's invalidSchemaOp, which api/block_pointers_test.go:101 already pins for a block-pointer refusal; the live room answers 409 DOC_SCHEMA on the next read, because a websocket frame carries no HTTP status. The refusal sentence is byte-identical on all three. Nothing was changed to match the acceptance line: the line is wrong for two of the paths, and the branch's behaviour is each route's own.

The forward merge's unchanged-diff fingerprint is not equal (0002d540... -> ac27c9e6...). It cannot be: the head adds T7's own commit, and the merge resolved five conflicted files whose branch-owned lines it necessarily rewrote. Both fingerprints are posted on the pull request.
